name: Enclomiphene

card.summary: The trans-isomer of clomiphene, studied for raising testosterone in men with secondary hypogonadism; forum use for appearance or height is largely untested.
card.note: Not approved by the FDA for any use; trials were in men with low testosterone, not for cosmetic or growth purposes.

quick.overview:
Enclomiphene is one of the two geometric isomers that make up clomiphene citrate, a drug long prescribed for female ovulatory dysfunction. It was developed as an oral treatment for men whose low testosterone stems from reduced pituitary signalling (secondary hypogonadism).

In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums it is discussed as a way to raise testosterone without injecting it, as a component of post-cycle protocols, and, in some threads, in relation to height or bone growth. Clinical trials exist for the hypogonadism use; none have tested it for appearance outcomes.
quick.mechanism: Enclomiphene blocks estrogen receptors in the hypothalamus and pituitary. Reduced estrogen feedback is reported to raise luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), which prompts the testes to make more testosterone themselves.
quick.risks: Published trials describe short-term safety comparable to placebo and testosterone gel, but long-term data are limited. Forum users report fatigue, mood effects and other complaints. Enclomiphene has no FDA approval, and products obtained outside prescriptions are of uncertain quality. Trial data in teenagers are absent.

lead: Enclomiphene (also enclomifene; trans-clomiphene; the citrate salt was developed under the name Androxal) is a non-steroidal selective estrogen receptor modulator that acts mainly as an estrogen receptor antagonist. It is the trans-isomer of clomiphene citrate, a drug prescribed since 1967 for ovulatory dysfunction in women [3][5][41]. People in physique and looksmaxxing communities are interested in it because higher testosterone is associated with muscle mass, leanness and the masculine features they are trying to build; the pill's appeal is that it is taken orally and, in trials, raised the body's own testosterone production rather than replacing it [7][11][24].

Its main investigated use is in men with secondary hypogonadism, where it increases the pituitary hormones LH and FSH and so prompts the testes to make more testosterone, while preserving sperm counts in trials that compared it with topical testosterone [3][7][38]. A 2025 meta-analysis of randomized trials of clomiphene or enclomiphene reported higher total testosterone, LH and FSH than placebo, with considerable heterogeneity [1]. A 2023 meta-analysis of men with obesity-related androgen deficiency found testosterone increases with both drugs [6].

Enclomiphene was never approved as a finished product by the FDA. The European Medicines Agency's committee recommended refusing marketing authorisation in 2018, and Wikipedia records that development was discontinued in 2021 [40]. In forums it is nonetheless discussed as a testosterone-raising option, as part of post-cycle or TRT-adjacent protocols, and by some posters in connection with height or bone growth, topics that no published trial has examined [24][25][28][30].

paras: Clomiphene citrate is a mixture of two geometric isomers, roughly 62 percent enclomiphene (trans) and 38 percent zuclomiphene (cis) [41]. Enclomiphene is the more antiestrogenic of the two; zuclomiphene has been described as predominantly estrogenic in early rodent work comparing the isomers [39][40]. Zuclomiphene is cleared much more slowly: about 10 hours is the figure given for the enclomiphene half-life, against several days to a week for zuclomiphene, and its accumulation was measured in women taking clomiphene [41][12]. Because of this difference, enclomiphene was proposed as a purer way to raise testosterone in men than the racemic mixture, and Wikipedia says purified enclomiphene was about twice as effective as the standard mix at boosting testosterone [3][41].

Clomiphene has been used off-label for many years in male hypogonadism, particularly where fertility is a concern [5]. Enclomiphene was developed to provide the antagonist activity without the zuclomiphene component [12][14]. It is metabolised in the liver, mainly by CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 [40].

sections.h: How people use it to improve their looks
paras: In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums, enclomiphene is discussed as a testosterone-raising option. Posters discuss testosterone in connection with muscle building, body composition, energy and mood, and describe taking enclomiphene orally as an alternative to injections [27][28][34][37]. Some describe using it in 'post-cycle' recovery after anabolic steroids or after stopping TRT, and others pair it with TRT to keep natural production going [31][32][34][35].

Teenage posters ask on looksmax.org whether it can help with puberty, height or bone growth. Replies in those threads commonly note that testosterone is not the main driver of bone length and that growth plates in older teens are mostly closed [24][25][29]. Users describe obtaining it through telehealth clinics and from overseas suppliers; the quality of non-prescription products has not been assessed in the published literature [37].

Clomiphene was synthesised in 1956 by a team led by Frank Palopoli at the William S. Merrell Chemical Company, and the FDA approved it in 1967 under the brand name Clomid [41]. Its two isomers were later separated and studied individually; rodent work comparing their estrogenic and antiestrogenic activity was published in 1981 [39].

Repros Therapeutics, formerly known as Zonagen, developed enclomiphene citrate as Androxal for men with low testosterone, and a phase III registration began in 2006 [20][42]. Phase II and III trials followed over the 2010s, including trials in overweight men with secondary hypogonadism [7][11][18]. Wikipedia records that by December 2016 the drug was in preregistration with the FDA and the EMA, that the EMA's CHMP recommended refusing marketing authorisation in January 2018 for secondary hypogonadism, and that development was discontinued for all indications in April 2021 [40]. Allergan announced in December 2017 that it would acquire Repros [42].

By blocking estrogen receptors at the hypothalamic-pituitary level, enclomiphene reduces negative feedback and is reported to increase LH and FSH release. The testes respond with increased testosterone production, an approach described as restoration of the body's own signalling rather than replacement with exogenous testosterone [3][11]. Wikipedia reports that it raises total and free testosterone without disproportionately raising dihydrotestosterone, though that statement is tagged as needing a citation [40].

A pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics study in men with secondary hypogonadism described the relationship between enclomiphene dosing and the testosterone, LH and FSH response [7]. Studies in women receiving clomiphene have measured serum concentrations of the two isomers across treatment cycles and found that both accumulate, without predicting ovulation response [12].

A 2013 Journal of Sexual Medicine report of a randomized open-label phase IIB study of 12 men compared oral enclomiphene with testosterone gel. Total testosterone at six months was similar in the two groups, LH and FSH rose only with enclomiphene, and sperm counts were raised in all men on enclomiphene who were measured while the gel did not raise counts above 20 million per mL in any of five men at three months [38].

A 2014 Fertility and Sterility phase II trial found that enclomiphene raised morning testosterone, estradiol and LH to levels similar to 1 percent testosterone gel while preventing the fall in sperm concentration seen with the gel [7]. A 2016 BJU International report described two phase III trials in overweight men aged 18 to 60 with secondary hypogonadism and morning testosterone at or below 300 ng/dL; testosterone rose over 16 weeks, LH and FSH increased with enclomiphene and fell with gel, and sperm concentration stayed in the normal range [11].

Further phase III registrations include a morning-testosterone normalisation study in overweight men (n=181), a safety study (n=499), an extension study (n=300) and a bone mineral density study (n=300) [18][22][21][17]. A phase II trial registered in 2016 examined body composition and metabolic parameters with diet and exercise in men with obesity and acquired hypogonadotropic hypogonadism [16]. A registered trial in male infertility was withdrawn [19].

A 2023 meta-analysis pooled seven studies with 292 men with obesity-related androgen deficiency; testosterone increases were 11.56 nmol/L with clomiphene and 7.50 nmol/L with enclomiphene, with no unexpected safety findings [6]. A 2025 meta-analysis of randomized trials reported a mean difference of about 274 ng/dL in total testosterone versus placebo, no significant difference from testosterone gel, and LH and FSH higher than with gel, with high heterogeneity [1].

A retrospective study of 66 men published in 2024 compared the two drugs and found median testosterone rose by 166 ng/dL with enclomiphene versus 98 ng/dL with clomiphene (not statistically different), while estradiol fell with enclomiphene and rose with clomiphene, and decreased libido, reduced energy and mood changes were reported less often with enclomiphene [13]. Reviews describe short-term safety as comparable to placebo and gel, and note a favourable effect on fasting glucose in early trials [3][13]. No published trial has examined enclomiphene for height, bone length, facial appearance or physique outcomes in healthy or adolescent males.

Reviews of the clinical trials describe short-term safety as satisfactory and similar to placebo and testosterone gel, while noting that long-term data are limited [3][5][13]. Wikipedia, citing pooled phase 2 and 3 data from 1,403 people, lists headache (1.6 percent), hot flush (1.1 percent), nausea (1.0 percent), muscle spasms (0.9 percent) and dizziness (0.7 percent), and records serious events including deep vein thrombosis (0.2 percent, three people), pulmonary embolism (one person) and one fatal ischemic stroke; it notes that SERMs are associated with thromboembolic risk [40]. Contraindications listed there include pregnancy, liver disease and uncontrolled adrenal or thyroid dysfunction [40].

Because the compound raises estradiol along with testosterone, trials measured estradiol, and some users attribute symptoms to estrogen changes [7]. Forum posts describe individual reports including fatigue and sleepiness, numbness or other genital sensations, and mood changes [26][36]. These are anecdotal and have not been verified in controlled studies.

Enclomiphene has not been approved by the FDA, and the EMA's CHMP recommended refusing marketing authorisation in January 2018 [40]. The FDA's pharmacy compounding advisory committee has considered enclomiphene, with an FDA media release comparing testosterone replacement with enclomiphene [40]. The parent drug, clomiphene, is prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency in category S4, hormone and metabolic modulators, and zuclomiphene can be detected in urine for months after use [41]. Anti-doping researchers have studied clomiphene metabolism [23].

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and physique communities
paras: On looksmax.org, enclomiphene is discussed under headings such as testosterone maxxing, usage by teenagers, and bone or height maxxing [24][25][28][29]. Posters frequently describe it as a way to raise testosterone without testicular shutdown and ask whether it affects growth plates or how to manage estrogen [24][25][29]. One thread title promises '90 99 percentile testosterone' [27].
On T Nation and similar forums, enclomiphene appears in discussions of TRT adjuncts, 'testosterone augmentation therapy', post-cycle therapy and stacks with other compounds [30][31][32][33][37].

Reviews list enclomiphene alongside selective androgen receptor modulators and novel testosterone formulations as an investigational approach to hypogonadism that may preserve fertility [4][14]. Clomiphene isomers have also been examined in unrelated laboratory contexts, such as antiviral activity in cell models [15].

timeline.event: Clomiphene is synthesised at the William S. Merrell Chemical Company [41].
Clomiphene is approved in the US as Clomid [41].
Rodent studies compare the estrogenic and antiestrogenic activity of enclomiphene and zuclomiphene [39].
A phase III registration of Androxal in men with secondary hypogonadism begins [20].
Randomized phase IIB study compares oral enclomiphene with testosterone gel in the Journal of Sexual Medicine [38].
A phase II randomized trial comparing enclomiphene with topical testosterone is published in Fertility and Sterility [7].
BJU International report of phase III trials in overweight hypogonadal men; the drug is under FDA and EMA review [11][40].
Allergan announces its acquisition of Repros Therapeutics [42].
The EMA's CHMP recommends refusing marketing authorisation for secondary hypogonadism [40].
Development is reported discontinued for all indications [40].
A meta-analysis of randomized trials of clomiphene and enclomiphene is published [1].

lore.intro: Forum discussions treat enclomiphene as a testosterone-raising tool, sometimes framed around puberty, height or post-cycle recovery [28][25].

claims.claim: Enclomiphene is a cleaner version of clomiphene because it lacks zuclomiphene.
claims.believers: Posters describe it as avoiding the long-lasting estrogenic isomer and so being better tolerated [31][35].
claims.experts: Reviews say zuclomiphene contributes little to the intended effect and persists longer; a retrospective study of 66 men found fewer libido, energy and mood complaints with enclomiphene, though testosterone gains did not differ significantly [14][13][41].

claims.claim: Enclomiphene can raise testosterone into a high percentile range.
claims.believers: Posters describe lab results after starting it and argue it works through the body's own signalling [27].
claims.experts: Trials in men with low testosterone report increases to the normal range; meta-analysis reports a large mean rise versus placebo, with high heterogeneity. Results in men with normal testosterone have not been established [1][7].

claims.claim: Enclomiphene can help height or bone growth.
claims.believers: Some users ask whether it could support bone maxxing; other posters reply that growth hormone, not testosterone, is the main route and that most plates are closed [24][25].
claims.experts: No published trial has tested enclomiphene for height or bone growth.

claims.claim: It is a safer alternative to testosterone because it preserves fertility and testicle size.
claims.believers: Users switching from TRT or HCG describe it as helping keep natural production and fertility [34][37].
claims.experts: Phase II and III trials report preserved sperm counts compared with topical testosterone, over short durations; long-term outcomes are not established [7][11].

claims.claim: Enclomiphene is useful in post-cycle therapy or after stopping TRT.
claims.believers: Posters describe it in recovery protocols, citing that it lacks zuclomiphene [31][35].
claims.experts: Published trials examined men with secondary hypogonadism, not recovery after anabolic steroid use.

claims.claim: Enclomiphene causes fatigue or estrogen spikes in some people.
claims.believers: Users report tiredness, numbness or low mood after starting it and suspect estrogen changes or poor product quality [26][36].
claims.experts: Trials reported raised estradiol alongside testosterone and described short-term safety as comparable to placebo; individual symptom reports have not been systematically studied [7][13].

claims.claim: It is suitable for teenagers going through puberty.
claims.believers: Threads by young posters ask how to use it at 15 or 16 and describe it as a puberty-support tool [25][29][28].
claims.experts: Trials were in adult men with secondary hypogonadism; the studies cited here did not enrol adolescents [5][7][11].

claims.claim: It is an approved prescription product.
claims.believers: Posters describe getting it through telehealth clinics [37].
claims.experts: The EMA's committee recommended refusing authorisation in 2018 and Wikipedia records development as discontinued in 2021; no FDA approval is reflected in the trial literature [40].

angle.goal: Muscle, leanness and masculine features (via testosterone)
chain: Blocks estrogen receptors in the hypothalamus and pituitary
Testosterone-dependent muscle, fat distribution and drive are discussed as benefits
angle.text: Users take enclomiphene hoping that higher natural testosterone will support muscle, leanness and energy for training, without the testicular suppression that comes with injected testosterone. Trials measured hormone levels in men with low testosterone; appearance outcomes were not the endpoint.
